title: Field retro + rapid response log — Jan 12 2027
content:
Meeting: Field Retro + Rapid Response
Date: 2027-01-12
Attendees: Marco Chen (owner), Aisha Patel (field eng), Liam O'Connor (SRE), Priya Rao (network lead), Diego Martinez (customer success)
Duration: 45m
Location: Zoom + on-site bridge (client: AtlasRetail)

Summary:
This doc captures the standup + rapid-response thread from the on-prem install at AtlasRetail (Seattle) that escalated yesterday evening. We ran a 2-hour off-hours mitigation, validated a temporary failover, and agreed on follow-ups to prevent recurrence.

High-level timeline:
- 2027-01-11 19:20 PST: Customer reports intermittent gRPC timeouts to inference nodes after kernel patching cycle.
- 2027-01-11 20:05 PST: Field eng (Aisha) collects node logs and sees repeated TCP RSTs + MTU-mismatch signs on the OOB NIC.
- 2027-01-11 21:10 PST: Root cause triage begins — suspected mismatch between customer switch MTU and host bonding.
- 2027-01-11 23:00 PST: Temporary mitigation applied (route-based failover, drop to 9000 -> 1500 MTU on secondary link) — customer throughput restored.
- 2027-01-12 09:00 PST: Retrospective + next steps scheduled.

Observations / Findings:
1) Networking: The primary issue was a split-horizon MTU configuration when the customer applied a firmware update to their leaf switches. The host-side bond had jumbo frames enabled (9000) but one switch port fell back to 1500 after the firmware reboot. Result: fragmented packets + device-level RSTs when NFS/HTTP kept large write windows open.
2) Kernel/IO: The firmware update also changed the RDMA driver binding order on the Mellanox NICs. That caused subtle failovers where RDMA attempted to use a link that had been administratively down for a short time. The inference runtime saw _long tail_ latency spikes rather than full crashes.
3) Mounts & Storage: NFS mounts experienced intermittent stalls; we saw duplicate NFS retransmits which compounded the tail latency for model loads.
4) Observability gap: Node-level metric (kernel drop counts + bond link-state-change events) were not being forwarded into the customer-facing dashboard within the required SLA window (5m). Our collector config had a 10m scrape interval for infra metrics on private installs by default.

Immediate actions performed during incident:
- Aisha: toggled bond mode to active-backup for suspect NICs, forced failover to the secondary fabric and validated model-serving processes resumed.
- Liam: rolled temporary policy to reduce scrape interval on the collector to 30s for the affected hostgroup and opened a hotfix on the telemetry agent.
- Priya: coordinated with AtlasRetail network team to pin the switch port MTU to 9000 and to hold firmware staging until we ship an installer MCA that validates switch configs.
- Diego: notified customer stakeholders and kept status page updated; scheduled an on-site follow-up for Friday.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Marco: Draft a small 'preflight check' module in the installer that validates switch MTU, bond settings, and RDMA driver bindings. Short-term checklist only. Due: 2027-01-19. Linked PR TODO: github.com/redwood-inference/installer #412 (WIP).
- Aisha: Produce a runbook fragment for 'MTU mismatch' that field eng can run in 15–20 minutes; include validate commands (ip link, ethtool, show interfaces, dmesg greps). Due: 2027-01-14.
- Liam: Release telemetry agent hotfix v1.2.3 to change default scrape interval policy for private installs to 60s for infra-critical metrics, and add an override flag in the installer. Due: 2027-01-21.
- Priya: Work with solutions engineering to add a 'switch firmware gating' note in the deployment playbook and recommend staging windows. Due: 2027-01-18.
- Diego: Coordinate post-mortem review with AtlasRetail on 2027-01-15; collect any additional network telemetry (sflow) from customer. Due: 2027-01-15.

Runbook / commands to include in Aisha's doc (draft snippets):
- Check bond and MTU:
  sudo ip -s link show bond0
  sudo ethtool -k eth0 | grep -i jumbo
  sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 9000
- Inspect dmesg for RST/segmentation signs:
  sudo dmesg | egrep -i "RST|MTU|fragment|mellanox|mlx5" --color=never | tail -n 200
- RDMA binding verification:
  ibstat || echo 'no ib devices'
  lsmod | egrep 'mlx5|rdma'
- NFS quick health check:
  sudo showmount -e 127.0.0.1
  sudo cat /proc/net/rpc/nfs | egrep -i 'retrans|timeout'

Proposed short-term mitigations for future installs:
- Add preflight gating in installer: verify MTU, bond mode, RDMA link states before moving to production mode.
- Change default telemetry scrape on private installs for infra metrics from 10m -> 60s (configurable).
- Add a bootstrap audit that records interface config to S3 (customer-owned) for first 24h after install to aid triage.

Longer-term improvements:
- Integrate network sanity checks into Redwood Console rollout flow where the install can optionally block deploys if network tests fail. This would be a new check in the rollout canary. (Product / Console follow-up).
- Add automated test harness for switch firmware updates in our test beds: run firmware update -> run internal model-serving load -> verify tail latency.

Risks & open questions:
- Does adding 60s scrapes significantly increase telemetry egress cost for large fleets on Dedicated/Private? Need cost estimate. (Liam to model).
- Will customers accept an installer that writes a temporary audit bundle to their S3? Need legal sign-off; privacy review. (Diego + Legal).
- Are there any NIC drivers/models we should block until we have validated RDMA behavior in our QA lab? (Research to compile a short list).

Follow-ups / Next meetings:
- Post-incident sync with AtlasRetail: 2027-01-15 10:00 PST (Diego owner).
- Install checklist review (internal): 2027-01-17 11:00 PST (Marco leads).
- Telemetry cost model review: 2027-01-18 (Liam leads).

Notes to self / field tips:
- When in doubt about post-firmware link behavior, flip bond to active-backup before experimenting with MTU changes. Active-backup isolates impact.
- Capture tc, iptables, and dmesg immediately and tag the archive with time-sync check (ntp/chrony) — we've hit time-drifted logs twice now.

Appendix: quick evidence snapshots (copied log excerpts sanitized)
- dmesg excerpt: "mlx5 0000:83:00.0: link state changed to DOWN due to admin down (eth0)"
- netstat excerpt: repeated TCP RST from 10.12.8.5 -> 10.12.8.112

If you have further notes or want me to add more log excerpts, drop them here. I'll update the installer PR checklist with the commands above and link it once ready.

-- Marco
